content: The Christopher and Dana Reeve Foundation (CDRF) is a nonprofit organization based in Short Hills, New Jersey, that is committed to advancing treatments and cures for paralysis caused by spinal cord injuries and other neurological conditions. Additionally, the foundation focuses on enhancing the quality of life for individuals living with disabilities. The organization originated from the American Paralysis Foundation, which was established in 1982. In 1995, following a horseback riding accident that left actor Christopher Reeve paralyzed and a quadriplegic, he became involved with the foundation. He provided financial support, lent his name to the cause, and eventually transformed it into the Christopher Reeve Paralysis Foundation, later renamed the Christopher Reeve Foundation. By early 2006, the foundation had distributed over $64 million in research grants and more than $8 million in quality-of-life grants. After Christopher Reeve passed away in October 2004, his wife, Dana Reeve, took over as Chair of the Foundation. Tragically, Dana Reeve succumbed to lung cancer 17 months later, in March 2006. Following her death, Peter D. Kiernan III assumed the role of Chair. On March 11, 2007, the foundation officially changed its name to the Christopher and Dana Reeve Foundation to honor the legacy of both Christopher and Dana Reeve. The name change was announced on the first anniversary of Dana Reeve’s passing and was intended to symbolize the partnership, courage, and compassion that the Reeves embodied. The mission of the Christopher and Dana Reeve Foundation is to find a cure for spinal cord injuries by supporting groundbreaking research. Additionally, the foundation aims to improve the lives of individuals living with paralysis through grants, advocacy, and the dissemination of information. In June 2006, the foundation launched a public awareness campaign called Superman Tags. This initiative involved selling dog tags featuring the iconic Superman S-Shield logo alongside the foundation’s motto, Go Forward. All proceeds from the sale of these tags were directed toward the foundation’s efforts to develop treatments and cures for paralysis. Warner Bros. generously allowed the foundation to use the Superman logo without royalties for the duration of the campaign, which concluded in February 2008. The foundation aspired to replicate the widespread success of the Lance Armstrong Foundation’s LIVESTRONG wristbands. Several celebrities participated in the campaign and were tagged, including Brandon Routh (who portrayed Superman in Superman Returns), Kate Bosworth (Lois Lane in Superman Returns), Dean Cain (Superman in Lois and Clark: The New Adventures of Superman), Erica Durance (Lois Lane in Smallville), David Boreanaz, Robin Williams, and Ray Romano. Christopher Reeve’s legacy continues to inspire and be remembered through these efforts.
